Lam Research.role: Leading supplier of etch and deposition tools critical to advanced logic and memory fabrication; strong moat but revenue is tied to cyclical WFE capex, driving moderate permanence and low capex elasticity.

KLA Corporation.role: KLA dominates semiconductor process control and inspection/metrology equipment with ~50%+ share, making it a high-moat but WFE-capex-cyclical supplier whose revenue depends on fab investment cycles.

Applied Materials.role: Leading supplier of wafer-fabrication equipment (deposition, etch, CMP) essential to building AI and advanced-logic chips; durable franchise but earnings are tied to cyclical fab capex spending.

Analog Devices.role: ADI is a leading analog/mixed-signal and power chipmaker serving industrial, automotive, and communications markets with broad diversification and strong design-win stickiness; it sits in AI-infra as a quality, moderately cyclical supplier with durable franchises but meaningful end-market sensitivit

NXP Semiconductors.role: NXP is a leading automotive and industrial semiconductor supplier with strong franchises in microcontrollers, processors, and secure connectivity; it sits in AI-infra as an edge-AI enabler but earnings are cyclical and tied to auto/industrial end-market demand, which is currently soft.

Microchip Technology.role: Broad-line supplier of 8/16/32-bit microcontrollers, analog and FPGA products to industrial, automotive and IoT markets; sits in defensive-cyclical territory given a sticky but inventory-sensitive embedded franchise recovering from a sharp downcycle.

ON Semiconductor.role: Leading supplier of power management and silicon carbide devices for EVs, ADAS and industrial power; sits as a cyclical AI-infra/automotive name whose near-term revenue is pressured by auto inventory digestion and softer EV demand despite a durable SiC franchise.

GlobalFoundries.role: Specialty foundry focused on differentiated nodes (RF, power, automotive, IoT) rather than leading-edge AI logic, giving it durable but cyclical end-market demand with modest growth and limited direct exposure to the AI compute boom.

Intel.role: Legacy x86 CPU leader attempting a costly foundry turnaround and AI accelerator pivot; sits mid-tier on quality and dominance given eroding share versus AMD/Nvidia/TSMC, heavy capex burden, and uncertain execution, making earnings durability cyclical rather than secular.

Lattice Semiconductor.role: Lattice is a fabless leader in small, low-power FPGAs serving industrial, comms, automotive and client-edge markets; it sits in AI-infra with moderate moat but cyclical exposure given recent inventory-driven revenue declines and dependence on broad semiconductor capex cycles.

Entegris.role: Supplies ultra-high-purity materials, filtration, and advanced deposition/CMP consumables essential to semiconductor fabrication; consumable-heavy model gives recurring revenue tied to wafer starts, but it remains exposed to semiconductor capex and utilization cycles.

MKS Instruments.role: MKS supplies subsystems and instrumentation (vacuum, lasers, RF power, photonics) critical to semiconductor fabrication and advanced packaging; it sits in AI-infra as a cyclical WFE-exposed enabler with solid niche moats but demand tied to volatile capex cycles and a leveraged balance sheet from the

Cadence Design Systems.role: Dominant EDA duopolist (with Synopsys) whose software is mission-critical and recurring for all chip designers; secular AI-driven design complexity supports durable demand, warranting low permanence risk and high quality despite a premium valuation.

Synopsys.role: Synopsys is a duopoly leader in electronic design automation software and IP essential to all advanced chip design, giving it recurring, high-margin revenue with deep moats; its demand is tied to secular semiconductor complexity rather than discretionary capex, so it sits as durable AI-infrastructur

Skyworks Solutions.role: Supplies RF front-end modules for smartphones and IoT, heavily exposed to Apple concentration and a mature, cyclical handset market, giving it modest growth and limited AI leverage despite stable cash flows.

Qorvo.role: Qorvo supplies RF front-end modules and filters primarily for smartphones (heavy Apple/Android exposure) plus defense and connectivity; it sits as a cyclical, mobile-concentrated semiconductor name with modest growth and limited direct AI leverage, hence moderate quality and elevated beta.

Allegro MicroSystems.role: Allegro designs magnetic (Hall-effect) and inductive sensor ICs plus power chips heavily levered to automotive electrification and ADAS; it holds strong niche share but sits in a cyclical auto/industrial end-market recovering from an inventory correction, hence moderate growth and mid-tier durabilit

Power Integrations.role: Power Integrations designs high-voltage power conversion semiconductors for consumer, industrial, and increasingly data-center/AI power delivery; it sits in AI-infra with moderate growth as a niche analog leader with real moat but meaningful cyclicality tied to consumer and industrial end markets.

Diodes Incorporated.role: Diodes makes commodity discrete and analog components for consumer, industrial, and automotive end-markets; it sits as a cyclical, fragmented-market supplier with limited AI-specific exposure and earnings tied to broad semiconductor demand cycles.

Cirrus Logic.role: Cirrus designs audio codecs and mixed-signal/power ICs, with heavy revenue concentration in Apple smartphones; it sits defensive-cyclical due to mature consumer-electronics end markets and single-customer exposure that caps growth and durability.

Photronics.role: Photronics is a leading independent maker of photomasks essential to chip fabrication; it sits in AI-infra as a critical supply-chain input but faces semiconductor cyclicality and only indirect AI leverage, warranting moderate growth and quality scores.

FormFactor.role: FormFactor is the leading supplier of advanced probe cards used in semiconductor wafer test, benefiting from HBM/AI chip complexity but exposed to cyclical test-capex and memory demand swings.

Axcelis Technologies.role: Supplier of ion implantation systems concentrated in mature-node power/automotive chips; cyclical WFE exposure and soft near-term semiconductor capex pressure revenue, giving it meaningful downside sensitivity despite a solid niche position.

Veeco Instruments.role: Veeco supplies deposition, laser annealing, and ion-beam systems to semiconductor and data-storage customers; it benefits from AI-driven capex cycles but is a cyclical niche equipment vendor with modest share versus larger WFE peers, so it sits as volatile, capex-elastic AI-infra.

CEVA.role: CEVA licenses DSP and edge-AI IP (wireless, sensing, connectivity) to chipmakers, earning royalties on shipped devices; a small-cap IP play with real design-win exposure but modest scale, cyclical royalty streams, and competition from larger IP vendors.

Palo Alto Networks.role: Leading enterprise cybersecurity vendor consolidating network, cloud, and SOC security into an AI-infused platform; recurring subscription revenue and non-discretionary spend make it durable, placing it as a high-quality AI-platform name rather than speculative.

Fortinet.role: Fortinet is a profitable network security leader with strong firewall franchise and recurring subscription revenue; it sits as a durable defensive name given non-discretionary security spend, though growth has decelerated from pandemic highs and competition in the space is intense.

Okta.role: Okta provides cloud identity and access management with recurring subscription revenue; durable demand and improving profitability place it as a quality mid-tier software name, though it faces stiff competition from Microsoft Entra and decelerating growth.

Elastic.role: Elastic provides search, observability, and security analytics software (Elasticsearch) increasingly positioned for vector search and RAG-based AI workloads; durable subscription revenue and a credible AI-search angle place it as a mid-quality AI-platform name with moderate moat but meaningful compe

Twilio.role: Twilio provides programmable communications APIs (messaging, voice, email) increasingly layered with AI-driven customer engagement; it sits in AI-platform with moderate growth, usage-based recurring revenue, and a defensible but competitive position in CPaaS.

DocuSign.role: DocuSign leads e-signature and is extending into AI-driven Intelligent Agreement Management with recurring SaaS revenue; modest single-digit growth and strong retention place it as a quality defensive name rather than a high-growth AI story.

Asana.role: Asana is a subscription work-management platform layering AI agents onto collaboration workflows; decelerating growth, persistent GAAP losses, and a crowded competitive field (Atlassian, Monday, Microsoft) place it in the speculative disruptive bucket with modest moat and elevated terminal risk.

UiPath.role: UiPath is a leading robotic process automation (RPA) platform pivoting toward agentic AI automation; it sits in AI-platform with moderate moat and recurring revenue, but faces slowing growth, intensifying competition, and uncertain monetization of its agent pivot.

Salesforce.role: Dominant enterprise CRM/SaaS platform layering AI agents (Agentforce) onto a large recurring-revenue base; durable subscription moat but mature mid-teens growth and uncertain AI monetization keep it in platform rather than hyper-growth territory.

Adobe.role: Dominant creative/document software franchise embedding Firefly generative AI into recurring subscriptions; durable cash flows and strong moat, but faces disruption risk from AI-native image/video tools pressuring pricing power.

Intuit.role: Intuit dominates SMB accounting (QuickBooks) and consumer tax (TurboTax) with AI features layered onto sticky recurring software; durable subscription revenue and a strong moat place it near the defensive end despite AI-platform ambitions.

Netflix.role: Leading global streaming platform using AI to drive recommendations, personalization, and content efficiency; a durable subscription franchise where AI is an optimization layer rather than the core revenue thesis, hence defensive positioning with modest growth.

Micron peer / Teledyne.role: Diversified industrial maker of imaging sensors, instrumentation, and aerospace/defense electronics; sits as a quality mid-cyclical with durable niche moats but modest growth and only partial AI-sensing exposure.

Flex.role: Flex is a diversified electronics manufacturing services provider whose data-center/cloud segment (power, racks, interconnect) rides AI capex, but thin EMS margins, cyclical hardware exposure and a fragmented competitive field place it mid-tier on moat and earnings durability.

Arrow Electronics.role: Broadline electronic components distributor that moves semiconductors and IP&E to OEMs and contract manufacturers; it sits in AI-infra as a low-margin, cyclical channel intermediary with thin pricing power and demand highly geared to end-market inventory cycles rather than secular AI capex.

TE Connectivity.role: Diversified connector and sensor maker whose high-speed interconnect products ride AI data center buildouts, but AI is only a slice of a largely cyclical industrial/auto-exposed business, so it sits as a moderate-quality AI-infra play.

Eaton.role: Diversified electrical equipment maker whose data-center power distribution, switchgear, and UPS products benefit from AI buildout; durable industrial franchise but exposed to capex cyclicality, hence moderate permanence and capex elasticity.

GE Vernova.role: Diversified power equipment maker (gas turbines, grid, wind) riding surging electricity demand from AI datacenters; strong gas/grid backlog but earnings remain partly cyclical and tied to utility/capex cycles rather than pure AI spend.

Constellation Energy.role: Largest US nuclear operator selling carbon-free baseload power via PPAs to hyperscalers for data centers; sits near defensive given recurring utility-like cash flows but carries AI-upside optionality, tempering its revenue growth and durable but regulated earnings.

Vistra.role: Independent power producer with a large nuclear and gas fleet benefiting from surging data-center electricity demand; sits as a quasi-defensive utility play with cyclical commodity/merchant-power exposure that tempers earnings durability and moat.

Johnson Controls.role: Diversified building-systems and HVAC provider whose thermal-management and liquid-cooling products ride data-center buildout; sits in AI-infra as a credible but indirect, partly-cyclical beneficiary rather than a pure-play.

Equinix.role: Equinix is the leading global interconnection and colocation REIT with recurring lease-based revenue and high switching costs; it sits in AI-infra as picks-and-shovels real estate for cloud/AI workloads, with durable recurring cash flows but modest growth and REIT-like valuation.

Digital Realty Trust.role: A global data center REIT leasing colocation and interconnection capacity benefiting from AI-driven demand; recurring lease income and physical infrastructure moat make it durable but REIT economics and rate sensitivity cap valuation and growth.

Oklo.role: Pre-revenue developer of small modular fast reactors targeting data-center power; speculative moonshot with no deployed plants and regulatory/execution risk, hence high beta and permanence despite a credible long-term nuclear TAM.

Broadcom peer / Oracle skip / MongoDB.role: Consumption-based cloud data warehouse/platform monetizing analytics and AI workloads on stored enterprise data; durable recurring revenue but faces hyperscaler and open-source competition, rich valuation, and usage sensitivity to customer IT budgets.

ARKK (ARK Innovation).role: disruptive-innovation basket LED BY TESLA (~10%), then AMD, CRISPR, Tempus AI, Robinhood. High beta, rich multiples, Tesla-driven idiosyncratic swings — NOT a semis basket.

QQQ (Nasdaq-100).role: Nasdaq-100 mega-cap tech; quality, but rich and tech-tilted.

VOO (S&P 500).role: broad US large-cap; the market itself — durable, diversified.

SCHD (Dividend).role: quality-dividend value basket; low beta, cheap, durable earnings.

DTCR (Data Ctr Infra).role: data-center REITs & digital infra (Equinix, Digital Realty, American Tower); physical, contracted, durable — low beta.

GRID (Smart Grid).role: grid/power equipment for the AI electricity demand (Eaton, Quanta, GE Vernova); inelastic infra spend.

NUKE (Nuclear/Uranium).role: nuclear/uranium for data-center baseload (Constellation, Vistra, Cameco, BWX); high-growth but cyclical/volatile.

VGT (Info Tech).role: broad US information-technology sector; mega-cap heavy, durable.

IGV (Software).role: application & infrastructure software basket; higher multiple, subscription-durable.
